questions.question: What does `if` actually check in Bash?
options: Whether the expression after it evaluates to the string "true"
The exit status of the command after it, where 0 means true
Whether the command printed any output
Whether the variable after it is non-empty
questions.explanation: if runs a command and branches on its exit status: 0 is success (true) and any non-zero status is false. That is why `if grep -q ERROR file` works.

questions.question: What does `[[ 10 > 9 ]] && echo true || echo false` print?
options: false, because > compares strings and "1" sorts before "9"
questions.explanation: Inside [[ ]], > and < are string comparisons. Use -gt or arithmetic (( 10 > 9 )) for numbers.

questions.question: A script runs `printf '1\n2\n' | while read -r l; do ((count++)); done` with count=0 beforehand. Why is count still 0 afterwards?
options: The while loop ran in a subshell because it was part of a pipeline, so its changes were lost
((count++)) does not work on variables set outside the loop
printf output cannot be piped into a loop
questions.explanation: Each part of a pipeline runs in a subshell. Feed the loop with a redirect or process substitution, `done < <(cmd)`, to keep it in the current shell.

questions.question: How should a Bash function hand back a computed string such as a total?
options: echo it and capture it with $(...)
export it from inside the function
questions.explanation: return only sets an exit status from 0 to 255. Data is passed back by printing it and capturing with command substitution, e.g. total=$(add 2 3).
